newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila's Napocor to negotiate pact with U.S. firms.
newsitem.headline: Manila's Napocor to negotiate pact with U.S. firms.

text.p: The Philippines National Power Corp (Napocor) board of directors has approved the power firm negotiating a power purchase agreement with a consortium of U.S.-based companies that has proposed building a 304-mw power plant.

"We have given the management the go-signal to negotiate with the San Pascual Cogeneration Co," Energy Minister and Napocor chairman Francisco Viray told reporters late on Monday after a board meeting.

San Pascual Cogeneration Co (SGCC), a consortium composed of Texaco Inc, Caltex Philippines Inc, and Mission Energy of the United States had submitted an unsolicited proposal to build the power plant near the Caltex refinery in Batangas, south of Manila.
Caltex is a unit of Caltex Petroleum Corp, which is a joint venture of Texaco Inc and Chevron Corp.
Under the law, Napocor had to allow other interested companies to match the consortium's solicited proposal. But no other firm submitted a competitive bid when it was offered last month.
The power plant is expected to be ready for commercial operation by 2001.
